tile-grout.$description: Tile Grout — Signature brand border and link accent — orange tile-line strokes that frame cards, links, and section edges with the warmth of fired clay against the clinical white canvas

cold-press-green.$description: Cold-Press Green — Primary action fill — the dark botanical green of filled CTA buttons, footer band, and category button backgrounds, signaling the product inside without resorting to food-photo greens

sticker-crimson.$description: Sticker Crimson — Hard-offset shadow accent — deep burgundy that throws a zero-blur 5px shadow under stickers and emphasized buttons, turning flat elements into screen-print layers peeled onto the page

noir.$description: Noir — Navigation, body text, and default border color — the unyielding black that carries every paragraph, icon stroke, and card hairline

glacial-white.$description: Glacial White — Page canvas, card surface, and reverse text on dark nav and green CTAs — the clinical white tile of the entire system

ash.$description: Ash — Soft card border and subtle fill — the gray grout between white surfaces, used for hairline dividers and recessed card frames

char.$description: Char — Heading color and deep-surface accent — nearly-black tone for the heaviest display text and occasional dark bands

concrete.$description: Concrete — Mid-gray utility border and muted body text — quieter dividers where full black would be too loud

fog.$description: Fog — Input field border — neutral resting-state outline for form fields

slate.$description: Slate — Input text and icon fill — secondary legibility gray for form labels and small icon detail

pewter.$description: Pewter — Decorative low-emphasis border and text — rarely used, appears on tertiary UI marks

helvetica.$description: All UI and editorial text. The choice of system Helvetica is deliberate — it reads as lab-label stencil rather than fashion-serif sophistication. Weight 900 headlines shout at 40-48px in all-caps with positive tracking, weight 400-500 carries body copy at 14-18px. No custom display face: the system itself is the brand.
